en: The Garland of Nine Jewels of Dakṣiṇāmūrti.

May that primordial splendor, whose crest is the young moon, abide in my heart—He who is served at the foot of the banyan tree by the foremost of sages; whose lotus-hands are folded in a special mudrā; who possesses a gentle smile, a sweet appearance, and noble majesty.
He is peaceful, white as the luster of the autumnal moon, with a face as delightful as the moon, wearing earrings of brilliance equal to the sun and moon, and clad in garments as pure as the moon.
I meditate in my heart, forever, upon the Teacher who grants desired aims—he who holds a lute, a book, a rosary, a bracelet, and the gesture of exposition in his hands.
I praise the Lord, whose body is like camphor, whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals, whose heart is cool as camphor, who is the play of compassion;
he who has the crescent moon as his crest-ornament, who is delightful with infinite virtues, and whose lotus feet are served by Indra and the other gods.
We meditate upon the Auspicious Ocean, who is seated upon a golden throne in a celestial chariot drawn by goats; whose arms are adorned with rings and whose body is noble;
who wears the moon, the lord of Rohiṇī, as his crest-ornament.
He resembles the rising sun, possesses three eyes, and is radiant with white unguents. He is youthful, wears a topknot, has a serene countenance, and stands at the foot of a banyan tree.

To the tawny-eyed Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who causes the young deer to stand still, whose form is like that of the sacred thread (*brahmasūtra*), who bestows fearlessness upon his devotees and removes their fear;
To Him, from even a mere fraction of whose compassion the ancient teachers—Śrī Kānta, Druhiṇa, Upamanyu, Tapana, Skanda, Indra, Nandi, and others—attained greatness;

To that Guru of all directions, whose body is beautiful, who is adorned with a gentle smile, whose lotus-hand is charming in its gesture of consciousness (*cinmudrā*), we place that auspicious One within our hearts.

One should meditate upon Śiva in the heart: wearing matted locks, adorned with the crescent moon, three-eyed, blazing like the moon, four-armed, the bestower of knowledge, holding a rosary, a book, and fire in his hands. One should likewise meditate on the Daughter of the Mountain seated upon his left thigh, embracing him; she is youthful, dark-complexioned, holding a blue lotus, resembling the moon, and gazing at Śiva.

I worship him who holds a book with one embraced hand, and with others a jar filled with nectar, the seal consisting of knowledge, and a rosary of pearls. (8) I salute that primordial Teacher, the sprout of the bliss of liberation, who dwells near the banyan tree and whose lotus-hands are marked by the seal of most excellent wisdom. (9)
Thus ends the hymn "The Garland of Nine Jewels" dedicated to the venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti.
